title: Consent
purpose: Read one participant's consent in one study: the current record and its answers, the participant's specimens and where their material went, the records history, withdrawals and reinstatements.
summary: One participant's consent in one study: the current record and answers, their specimens, where their material went, and the history of records and withdrawals.

tasks.title: Act on a withdrawal in effect
steps: Select [[Hold withdrawn specimens]] when specimens lack its hold.
Use [[Record follow-up]] on each shipment that carried the participant's material.

tasks.title: Fix a transcription error
steps: Select [[Correct consent]]. The earlier version stays.

tasks.title: Record a re-consent
steps: Select [[Record consent]]. The participant and study are filled in.

good_to_know: Specimens registered after a withdrawal are not held automatically. Hold withdrawn specimens covers them.
Escalate to destruction and Request disposal of held specimens are in [[More]].
Whoever recorded the withdrawal, its escalation or the new consent cannot reinstate it.

sections.title: Notices
paragraphs: When a withdrawal that stops use is in effect, a notice shows its current instruction, effective date and recorder. After an escalation these facts come from the destruction instruction. If specimens in custody lack a hold from the withdrawal, a second notice gives the count. The distribution gate still blocks those specimens.

items.label: Form, Decision recorded, Date of the decision, Who decided, How it was documented
Where the original is filed
items.description: Where the signed or electronic original is kept.

items.label: Recorded
items.description: Who recorded the current record and when.

items.label: Restrictions
items.description: Opens to show the recorded restrictions; shown, never interpreted.

sections.title: Answers per category
paragraphs: Each category the form asks, with the answer recorded: Permitted, Refused or Not addressed, and whether the category governs use. A refusal answers no categories.

items.label: Specimens in custody
items.description: Available or exhausted specimens of the participant in every collection the study governs or has governed (a link that has ended included), each marked Held or Not held by the withdrawal in effect; the ID opens the specimen.

items.label: Open allocations
items.description: Allocations of those specimens still allocated or picked, with the request. After a withdrawal, allocations not yet picked are released; picked ones stay until staff put them back.

items.label: Distributed material
items.description: Dispatched shipments that carried the participant's material in the study: recipient, specimens, the agreement and what it says about the end of use and onward transfer, and the follow-ups recorded. The software sends nothing and recalls nothing.

items.label: Record follow-up
items.description: Admin and manager, while a withdrawal that stops use is in effect: records what was done about that shipment's material.

sections.title: Records
paragraphs: Every record of this consent, oldest first: Consent recorded, New consent recorded (re-consent) or Record corrected, with who, when, the reason and the answers. A correction lists each changed value with the earlier value struck through.

sections.title: Withdrawals and reinstatements
paragraphs: Each original withdrawal shows its kind, state (In effect, Do not contact, Reinstated), effective date, when and how it was received, the counts it held, released and found distributed at the time, who recorded it with the reason, and any reinstatement. Open Escalated to destruction on the original row to see the later instruction's effective date, receipt time and channel, recorder, recording time and reason.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: The newest 50 audit events of the consent, oldest first.

sections.title: Actions
paragraphs: Every staff role (admin, manager, technician, viewer) can open this page. Only admin and manager see and can use the buttons that change records; the server refuses the change to anyone else.

While a withdrawal is in effect the primary button is the next step: Hold withdrawn specimens when specimens lack a hold, otherwise Reinstate consent. A consented or refused consent has no primary button; Record consent (re-consent) and Correct consent are secondary. An action unavailable now is shown disabled with the reason.

items.label: Withdraw consent
items.description: Records a withdrawal. While withdrawn only a withdrawal of contact can be added.

items.label: Correct consent
items.description: Corrects a transcription error in the current record; the earlier version stays.

items.label: Record consent
items.description: A new record (re-consent), with the participant and study filled in.

items.label: More: Hold withdrawn specimens
items.description: Shown when specimens in custody lack a hold from the withdrawal in effect.

items.label: More: Escalate to destruction
items.description: Available for an active No further use withdrawal. It records the later destruction instruction on that withdrawal and leaves its holds in effect. After escalation the menu item is disabled and disposal requests are available for held specimens.

items.label: More: Request disposal of held specimens
items.description: Shown when the withdrawal originally asked for destruction or was escalated. Each disposal request needs approval by another person with disposal approval.

items.label: More: Reinstate consent
items.description: Ends the withdrawal and releases its holds. The recorders of the withdrawal, its escalation and the current consent record made after the withdrawal cannot reinstate it. If consent was recorded between withdrawal and escalation, record or correct the consent after escalation before reinstating.
